section_title: Punishment for theft
summary: Simple theft (dishonestly taking movable property out of someone's possession without consent, without force). Verified against primary source text.
cognizable: commonly cited as cognizable (secondary sources) — not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
bailable: commonly cited as bailable (secondary sources) — not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
punishment_range: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 3 years, or with fine, or with both. [Verified against primary source text]

section_title: Theft in dwelling house, etc.
summary: Theft committed in any building, tent, or vessel used as a human dwelling or for the custody of property — relevant if a theft occurred inside a home, shop, or similar structure. Verified against primary source text.
cognizable: commonly cited as cognizable (secondary sources) — not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
bailable: commonly cited as non-bailable given the higher penalty band (secondary sources) — not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
punishment_range: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 7 years, and liable to fine. [Verified against primary source text]

section_title: Robbery — definition
summary: Theft becomes robbery when the offender, in committing the theft, voluntarily causes or attempts to cause death, hurt, wrongful restraint, or fear of instant death/hurt/restraint. Extortion becomes robbery when committed in the victim's presence by putting them in fear of instant death or hurt. Verified against primary source text.
cognizable: commonly cited as cognizable (secondary sources) — not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
bailable: commonly cited as non-bailable (secondary sources) — not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
punishment_range: See section 392 for punishment.

section_title: Punishment for robbery
summary: Punishment for robbery as defined in section 390. A higher band applies to robbery committed on a highway. Verified against primary source text.
cognizable: commonly cited as cognizable (secondary sources) — not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
bailable: commonly cited as non-bailable (secondary sources) — not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
punishment_range: Rigorous imprisonment for a term of not less than 3 years nor more than 10 years, and liable to fine; if the robbery is committed on the highway, imprisonment may extend to 14 years. [Verified against primary source text]

section_title: Theft, including theft in/from a building or vehicle
summary: Vehicle theft is prosecuted under the general theft provisions (s.379); s.380 applies if the vehicle was taken from inside a building/dwelling/garage. No standalone 'vehicle theft' offense exists in the PPC itself — check for provincial motor-vehicle ordinances too, which were not researched here.
cognizable: commonly cited as cognizable (secondary sources) — not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
bailable: s.379: commonly cited as bailable; s.380: commonly cited as non-bailable (secondary sources) — neither independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
punishment_range: s.379: up to 3 years / fine / both. s.380: up to 7 years + fine. [Both verified against primary source text — see the Robbery/Theft entries above for the same sections]

section_title: Kidnapping — definition
summary: "Kidnapping is of two kinds: Kidnapping from Pakistan and kidnapping from lawful guardianship." Verified against primary source text (verbatim).
cognizable: not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
bailable: not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
punishment_range: See section 363 for the base punishment.

section_title: Punishment for kidnapping
summary: Base punishment for kidnapping a person from Pakistan or from lawful guardianship (section 359). Verified against primary source text.
cognizable: commonly cited as cognizable (secondary sources) — not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
bailable: commonly cited as non-bailable (secondary sources) — not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
punishment_range: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 7 years, and liable to fine. [Verified against primary source text]

section_title: Kidnapping or abducting in order to murder
summary: Kidnapping/abducting a person so that they may be murdered, or put in danger of being murdered. Verified against primary source text.
cognizable: commonly cited as cognizable (secondary sources) — not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
bailable: commonly cited as non-bailable given imprisonment-for-life exposure (secondary sources) — not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
punishment_range: Imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to 10 years, and liable to fine. [Verified against primary source text]

section_title: Kidnapping/abducting with intent secretly and wrongfully to confine a person
summary: Kidnapping/abducting a person with intent to cause them to be secretly and wrongfully confined. Verified against primary source text.
cognizable: commonly cited as cognizable (secondary sources) — not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
bailable: commonly cited as non-bailable (secondary sources) — not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
punishment_range: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 7 years, and liable to fine. [Verified against primary source text]

section_title: Kidnapping or abduction for extorting property, valuable security, etc.
summary: Abduction for the purpose of extorting property or a valuable security from the person kidnapped or from any person interested in them — the section most relevant to a kidnapping-for-ransom scenario. Verified against primary source text.
cognizable: commonly cited as cognizable (secondary sources) — not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
bailable: commonly cited as non-bailable given the death/life-imprisonment exposure (secondary sources) — not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
punishment_range: Death, or imprisonment for life, and liable to forfeiture of property. [Verified against primary source text]

section_title: Assault — definition
summary: A gesture or preparation intending or knowing it likely to cause a person present to apprehend imminent criminal force. Mere words alone do not amount to assault, though words can give a gesture that meaning. Verified against primary source text.
cognizable: not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
bailable: not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
punishment_range: See section 352 for punishment.

section_title: Punishment for assault or criminal force otherwise than on grave provocation
summary: Base punishment for assault (section 351) or use of criminal force, where the offender was not gravely and suddenly provoked by the victim. Verified against primary source text.
cognizable: commonly cited as non-cognizable (secondary sources) — not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
bailable: commonly cited as bailable (secondary sources) — not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
punishment_range: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 3 months, or fine which may extend to PKR 1,500, or both. [Verified against primary source text]

section_title: Shajjah (head/face injury) — classification only, not the punishment section
summary: IMPORTANT CORRECTION from an earlier draft of this knowledge base: Section 337 defines six graded categories of head/face wound (Shajjah), from a wound without exposing bone up to a skull fracture rupturing the brain membrane. Section 338 is NOT a general 'hurt' provision as previously assumed — it defines Isqat-i-Haml (causing a miscarriage), an unrelated offense. The PPC's 'hurt' framework (covering assault injuries generally) spans many further lettered sub-sections (337-A through 337-N and others) that were not individually verified here. Which sub-section and punishment applies to a given injury depends on its exact medical classification — this genuinely requires a doctor's assessment and a lawyer's read of the specific facts, not an automated match.
cognizable: varies by sub-clause — not verified here
bailable: varies by sub-clause; some grades are reported as non-bailable where Qisas cannot be enforced — not independently verified here
punishment_range: Not resolved to a specific figure — varies by the exact hurt sub-clause, which was not individually verified. Do not treat any single number as authoritative for a hurt/injury case; consult a lawyer.
source_citation: http://www.pljlawsite.com/html/ppc337.htm ; http://www.pljlawsite.com/html/ppc338.htm (both checked 2026-09-13 — 338 confirmed to be Isqat-i-Haml, not hurt grading)

section_title: Electronic forgery
summary: Interfering with or using an information system, device, or data with intent to cause damage/injury, make an illegal claim, or commit fraud by inputting, altering, deleting, or suppressing data so it is treated as authentic. Verified against primary source text.
cognizable: non-cognizable [verified: PECA s.43(1) — all offences non-cognizable/bailable/compoundable except ss.10, 21, 22 and their abetment]
bailable: bailable [verified: PECA s.43(1)]
punishment_range: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 3 years, or fine which may extend to PKR 250,000, or both. If committed against critical infrastructure: imprisonment up to 7 years or fine up to PKR 5,000,000, or both. [Verified against primary source text]
source_citation: https://sja.gos.pk/assets/Acts_Ordinances_Rules2/PEC2016.pdf, Section 13 and Section 43 (verified 2026-09-13 via direct PDF text extraction)

section_title: Electronic fraud
summary: With intent for wrongful gain, interfering with or using an information system/device/data, or inducing/deceiving a person, in a way likely to cause damage or harm — the section most relevant to online financial scams. Verified against primary source text.
cognizable: non-cognizable [verified: PECA s.43(1)]
bailable: bailable [verified: PECA s.43(1)]
punishment_range: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to 2 years, or fine which may extend to PKR 10,000,000, or both. [Verified against primary source text]

section_title: Cyber stalking
summary: With intent to coerce, intimidate, or harass, using an information system to repeatedly contact someone against clear disinterest, monitor their electronic communications, watch/spy in a way causing fear or distress, or share their photo/video without consent in a harmful manner. Verified against primary source text.
cognizable: non-cognizable [verified: PECA s.43(1)]
bailable: bailable [verified: PECA s.43(1)]
punishment_range: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to 3 years, or fine which may extend to PKR 1,000,000, or both. If the victim is a minor: up to 5 years or fine up to PKR 10,000,000, or both. [Verified against primary source text]

section_title: Offences against dignity of a natural person
summary: Intentionally and publicly exhibiting, displaying, or transmitting information known to be false, that intimidates or harms a person's reputation or privacy. Does not apply to licensed broadcast media content. Verified against primary source text.
cognizable: non-cognizable [verified: PECA s.43(1) — s.20 is not in the exception list (10, 21, 22)]
bailable: bailable [verified: PECA s.43(1)]
punishment_range: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to 3 years, or fine which may extend to PKR 1,000,000, or both. [Verified against primary source text]

section_title: Offences against modesty of a natural person and minor
summary: Publicly exhibiting/transmitting sexually explicit superimposed images, sexually explicit images/videos of a person, sexual intimidation, or enticing someone into a sexually explicit act via an information system, to harm, take revenge, create hatred, or blackmail. A separate, higher band applies if the victim is a minor, and a repeat offence against a minor carries a mandatory 10-year term. This is one of only three PECA sections (10, 21, 22) that is non-bailable and cognizable rather than the Act's general default. Verified against primary source text.
cognizable: cognizable [verified: PECA s.43(2) — s.21 is explicitly listed as non-bailable, non-compoundable, and cognizable by the investigation agency]
bailable: non-bailable [verified: PECA s.43(2)]
punishment_range: Base offence: imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine up to PKR 5,000,000, or both. If the victim is a minor: imprisonment up to 7 years and fine up to PKR 5,000,000. A repeat offence against a minor: imprisonment of 10 years and fine. [Verified against primary source text — note this corrects an earlier draft that stated a flat 7-year figure for the whole section]

section_title: Insulting modesty or causing sexual harassment
summary: Covers (1) words, sounds, gestures, or objects intended to insult a woman's modesty or intrude on her privacy, and (2) sexual advances/demands including verbal, written, or physical conduct that annoys, insults, intimidates, or threatens a person, including workplace harassment (which can extend beyond the physical workplace and normal working hours). Verified against primary source text.
cognizable: commonly cited as bailable/non-cognizable in secondary sources — not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
bailable: commonly cited as bailable (secondary sources) — not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
punishment_range: Imprisonment which may extend to 3 years, or fine which may extend to PKR 500,000, or both. [Verified against primary source text — note this corrects an earlier draft's much lower, unverified fine figure]
source_citation: http://www.pljlawsite.com/html/ppc509.htm equivalent text (verified 2026-09-13 via pakarbiter.com mirror content)

section_title: Intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of the peace
summary: Deliberately insulting another person, intending or knowing it is likely to cause them to break the public peace or commit another offence. Verified against primary source text.
cognizable: commonly cited as non-cognizable (secondary sources) — not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
bailable: commonly cited as bailable (secondary sources) — not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
punishment_range: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 2 years, or fine, or both. [Verified against primary source text]

section_title: Punishment for criminal intimidation
summary: Threatening another with injury to person, reputation, or property, with intent to cause alarm or to compel them to act (or not act) against their will. A higher band applies where the threat is to cause death, grievous hurt, destruction of property by fire, an offence punishable by death/life imprisonment/7+ years, or to impute unchastity to a woman. Verified against primary source text.
cognizable: commonly cited as non-cognizable for the base offence (secondary sources) — not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
bailable: commonly cited as bailable for the base offence (secondary sources) — not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
punishment_range: Base: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 2 years, or fine, or both. Aggravated forms listed above: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 7 years, or fine, or both. [Verified against primary source text]

section_title: Penalty for breach of an interim or protection order by the respondent
summary: A breach of a protection order or interim protection order (issued under section 11) by the respondent is itself a separate offence. The Act explicitly overrides the default CrPC classification for this specific offence. Verified against primary source text.
cognizable: cognizable [verified: Act s.15(2) — 'Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code the offence under this section shall be cognizable, bailable and compoundable']
bailable: bailable [verified: Act s.15(2), same citation]
punishment_range: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 1 year, or fine which may extend to PKR 20,000, or both. [Verified against primary source text]
source_citation: https://sindhlaws.gov.pk/setup/publications_SindhCode/PUB-NEW-18-000141.pdf, Section 15 (verified 2026-09-13 via direct PDF text extraction)

section_title: Punishment for the underlying domestic-violence offences listed in section 5
summary: Most section 5 sub-offences (physical/emotional/psychological/economic abuse etc., clauses a,b,c,d,e,g,h,i,n) are punished under the Pakistan Penal Code itself, not this Act. A few specific clauses carry their own standalone penalty: 5(f) — minimum 6 months imprisonment or compensation-fine of at least PKR 10,000, or both; 5(k) stalking — simple imprisonment of at least 1 year or compensation-fine of at least PKR 20,000, or both; 5(l) — imprisonment of either description of at least 2 years or compensation of at least PKR 50,000, or both; 5(m) — imprisonment of either description of at least 1 month, or fine, or both. Verified against primary source text.
cognizable: varies — most of these route to the underlying PPC offence's classification (see the corresponding PPC entries); not separately verified for each sub-clause
bailable: varies — see note above
punishment_range: See summary for the sub-clause-specific figures. [Verified against primary source text]

section_title: False information with intent to cause a public servant to use his lawful power to the injury of another person
summary: Knowingly giving false information to a public servant (including police), intending or knowing it likely to cause that public servant to act (or omit to act) improperly, or to injure/annoy someone — this is the provision behind the false-reporting notice shown before every submission (Step 6), regardless of the report's category.
cognizable: not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
bailable: commonly cited as bailable (secondary sources) — not independently confirmed against CrPC Schedule II primary text
punishment_range: Base: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 6 months, or fine (or both, per general secondary-source paraphrase). If the falsely-alleged offence is punishable by death: imprisonment may extend to 7 years. If punishable by life imprisonment: up to 5 years. For other offences: up to one-fourth of the longest term prescribed for that offence. [Base term and the escalation structure verified against primary source text; the exact wording of the base fine amount was not independently confirmed]
